report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Reap branches with provenance checks; commit and status helpers for allocated worktrees.

symbols.name: reap_branches
symbols.note: Deletes branches only when both in-process allocation and git reachability prove safety; reports per-allocation outcomes; raises RuntimeError on delete failures.

symbols.name: _forget_allocation
symbols.note: Removes allocation from in-memory dict and on-disk record.

symbols.name: _report_unverifiable_records
symbols.note: Lists on-disk allocation records not allocated in this process; never acts on them; omits all file fields.

symbols.name: _refs_containing
symbols.note: Returns refs other than the excluded branch whose history contains a given sha; fails closed on git errors.

symbols.name: _delete_unused_branch
symbols.note: Deletes a branch with -d first, then -D only if tip unchanged since proof.

symbols.name: commit_candidate
symbols.note: Stages and commits all changes in an allocated worktree; optional author.

symbols.name: has_changes
symbols.note: Returns whether an allocated worktree has changes via git status --porcelain.

claims.text: Reaping is a separate act, run by whoever knows the attempt is fully resolved.
claims.why: This method does not resolve intents; it only deletes branches after checking allocation and reachability, and the docstring explains the separation.

claims.text: A branch is deleted only when BOTH hold: 1. THIS manager object allocated it, in THIS process (:attr:`_allocations`, written by :meth:`create_worktree`), its worktree has been through :meth:`cleanup_worktree`, and its tip is byte-identical to the sha this manager itself read from git at allocation time. Nothing on disk contributes to this.
claims.why: The loop only considers allocations from self._allocations, requires allocation['worktree_removed'] (set by cleanup_worktree), and compares tip from git rev-parse to allocation['branch_tip_at_creation'].

claims.text: 2. Some OTHER ref still contains that tip, so deleting the branch orphans no commit. This is git's answer, not ours
claims.why: holders = self._refs_containing(tip, excluding=branch) is consulted and must be non-empty before deletion.

claims.text: a branch leaked by a CRASHED run is never reaped, because the process that could vouch for it is gone
claims.why: Only allocations in self._allocations (in-memory) are considered; on-disk records without a matching in-memory allocation are reported as unverifiable and never acted on.

claims.text: Records left on disk are reported as ``unverifiable`` and acted on by nobody.
claims.why: _report_unverifiable_records() appends rows with action 'unverifiable' and does not delete or modify them.

claims.text: Returns: One dict per allocation examined, with ``branch``, ``action`` (``deleted`` / ``retained`` / ``absent`` / ``pending`` / ``unverifiable``) and ``reason``.
claims.why: Each report dict contains 'branch', 'action', 'reason' (and 'path'/'record' in some rows); actions include all listed values.

claims.text: Raises: RuntimeError: If any branch that was cleared for deletion could not be deleted. Every allocation is still examined first; the failures are reported together rather than aborting on the first one.
claims.why: Failures are collected in a list and raised after the loop; the loop continues past each failure.

claims.text: Never acts on them. Reported rather than ignored so the leak is visible; reported WITHOUT any field parsed out of the file
claims.why: The method only returns rows with branch=None, path=None and does not parse file contents; it never modifies or deletes records.

claims.text: Refs OTHER than ``refs/heads/<excluding>`` whose history holds ``sha``.
claims.why: The function filters out the excluded ref by casefolded comparison and returns all other refs from for-each-ref --contains.

claims.text: A FAILED CALL IS NOT AN ANSWER. ... none of them may license a delete.
claims.why: except RuntimeError returns [] and the caller retains the branch when holders is empty.

claims.text: Compared case-INSENSITIVELY although git refs are case-sensitive: the only effect of a spurious match is that a ref is dropped from the holder list, which retains the branch.
claims.why: The excluded ref is casefolded and compared casefolded; a spurious match removes a ref from holders, causing retention.

claims.text: ``-d`` is tried first so git's own merged-check applies. If git refuses anyway -- it compares against the current HEAD, which may have moved somewhere unrelated -- the sha proof (re-taken here, so the branch cannot have moved in between) is what authorises ``-D``. The force flag is never reached without that proof.
claims.why: The method tries git branch -d first; on failure re-reads tip and compares to proven_tip before -D.

claims.text: The path is proven to be an allocated worktree first: a swapped directory would otherwise turn ``git add -A`` + ``git commit`` into a commit of the developer's working tree.
claims.why: target = self._require_allocated_worktree(path) is called before any git commands.

claims.text: Return whether the candidate worktree differs from its HEAD.
claims.why: Returns bool(self._run_git("status", "--porcelain", cwd=target)); empty output means no changes, non-empty means changes.

observations.what: reap_branches checks allocation['worktree_removed'] but does not verify that cleanup_worktree actually ran in this process; it relies on the in-memory flag set by cleanup_worktree, which is consistent with the trust model.

_refs_containing uses casefold on git refs; a branch named 'Feature' and 'feature' are distinct in git but treated as same here, potentially dropping a holder and retaining the branch -- aligned with fail-closed direction.
commit_candidate stages with 'add -A' which includes deletions and untracked files; if the worktree contains submodules or ignored files, behavior may differ, but no claim in the docstring pins that.

risks: reap_branches | low | Relies on cleanup_worktree having set worktree_removed; if cleanup_worktree is bypassed, a worktree still in use could be reaped. | Check whether cleanup_worktree is always called before reap_branches in the intended flow.
